column1: # Editing: word breaks, backspace, enter, tab, punctuation, digits.
# An unbroken English word with a repeated `a` is not a no-op: typing the
# second one two keys later re-marks the first vowel and drops what is between
# them (banana -> bânna, cacao -> câco, mama -> mâm). Upstream 2.0.3 does the
# same on macOS (DL-026). Recorded as the engine behaves, not as it ought to;
# `tests/corpus/README.md` rule 2's `xfail:` ids need comparator support that
# does not exist yet, so these are pinned as matches instead of silenced.
# Any of these ends the word and is then inserted literally: the mark already
# applied to the syllable stays (Engine.cpp's bracket/punctuation branches).
# A literal backslash is an ordinary character; `\\b` in the input column is
# the two-character sequence, not a backspace. This is the case the judge could
# not express before its expected column was decoded like the input column.
